text: Every Indian kitchen counts the whistles.
But what is actually happening inside the cooker?
As the water heats up, it turns into steam.
The rubber gasket seals the lid, so the steam has nowhere to go.
Pressure builds up, to almost double the air outside.
And under that pressure, water boils at around one hundred and twenty degrees, not one hundred.
That is why your dal cooks in minutes.
On top, a heavy weight sits on a tiny steam vent.
When the pressure gets strong enough, it lifts the weight, and the steam rushes out.
And if that vent ever gets blocked, a safety valve melts open first.
So every whistle is your cooker letting off extra pressure.
Send this to the person who counts them.
